title: State Commission's Obligation to Entertain Complaints Based on Value

content.scenario: A consumer purchases a product worth Rs. 5 crores and files a complaint with the State Commission, alleging defects in the product. The company disputes the Commission's jurisdiction, claiming the value of the product is beyond its limits.
content.outcome: The State Commission must entertain the complaint since the value of the goods or services paid as consideration (Rs. 5 crores) exceeds Rs. 1 crore but does not exceed Rs. 10 crores, as per section 47(1)(a)(i) of the Consumer Protection Act, 2019.

user_queries: What is the jurisdiction of the State Commission based on the value of goods or services?
Can the State Commission entertain complaints beyond Rs. 10 crores?
How does the State Commission determine the value of goods or services for jurisdictional purposes?
